forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: gets() performs no bounds checking and always causes a buffer overflow vulnerability.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace gets() with std::getline(std::cin, str) for C++ code, or fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), stdin) for C-style I/O.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: strcpy() performs no bounds checking and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with std::string assignment, or use strlcpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) when C-style char arrays are required.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: strcat() performs no bounds checking and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with std::string concatenation (+=) or strlcat(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) for C-style buffers.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: sprintf() has no output length limit and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), ...) or std::ostringstream for safe string formatting.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / DISA STIG: system() invokes a shell and is vulnerable to command injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace system() with execve() using an explicit argument array, or use a platform-safe alternative like boost::process.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / DISA STIG: popen() invokes a shell and is vulnerable to command injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use pipe()/fork()/execve() directly, or a safe process library, to avoid shell interpretation.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-90A: rand() and srand() are not cryptographically secure.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use std::random_device with std::mt19937 for general randomness, or a FIPS-validated DRBG (e.g., OpenSSL RAND_bytes()) for security operations.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-252 / OWASP A05: Raw new without nullptr check can result in uncaught bad_alloc or null pointer dereference.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use smart pointers (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr) instead of raw new to ensure automatic memory management and exception safety.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-704 / OWASP A05: reinterpret_cast bypasses the type system and can enable undefined behavior.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Prefer static_cast or dynamic_cast. Use reinterpret_cast only with careful documentation of the safety invariants.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / STIG V-222645: MD5 is cryptographically broken and not FIPS-compliant.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with SHA-256 (EVP_sha256()) via the OpenSSL EVP interface.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-131A: SHA-1 is deprecated and not FIPS 140-3 compliant.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with SHA-256 (EVP_sha256()) or stronger.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded password detected in C++ source.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove hardcoded passwords. Read credentials from secure environment variables or an encrypted configuration file.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: vsprintf() has no output length limit and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args) or std::ostringstream.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-001760 / CWE-120: These functions perform no bounds checking on %s specifiers and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with std::cin >> with explicit limits, or std::getline(std::cin, str) for line input.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-002560 / CWE-134: Passing a non-literal format argument to printf() enables format string attacks — attackers can read memory, overwrite addresses, or crash the program.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use std::print (C++23) or always pass a string literal as the format argument: printf("%s", msg) not printf(msg).

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-002560 / CWE-134: Passing a non-literal format argument to fprintf() enables format string attacks — attackers can read memory, overwrite addresses, or crash the program.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Always pass a string literal as the format argument: use fprintf(stream, "%s", msg) not fprintf(stream, msg).

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-002560 / CWE-134: Passing a non-literal format argument to syslog() enables format string attacks — attackers can read memory, overwrite addresses, or crash the program.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Always pass a string literal as the format argument: use syslog(priority, "%s", msg) not syslog(priority, msg).

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-401 / NIST SP 800-53 SA-15: C-style heap allocation bypasses RAII and requires manual memory management, leading to memory leaks and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with std::make_unique<T>() or std::make_shared<T>() for automatic, exception-safe memory management.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-401 / NIST SP 800-53 SA-15: Raw free() bypasses RAII and is prone to double-free and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use RAII and smart pointers (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr) to ensure automatic, deterministic memory release.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-401 / NIST SP 800-53 SA-15: Manual delete/delete[] bypasses RAII and is susceptible to double-free and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace raw new/delete pairs with std::make_unique or std::make_shared for exception-safe, leak-free resource management.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-190 / CWE-252: These functions provide no error detection for invalid input and have undefined behavior on overflow — they silently return 0 for invalid input.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with std::from_chars (C++17) for error-detecting number parsing, or std::stoi/std::stol with exception handling.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-663 / POSIX: strtok() uses hidden internal static state and is not thread-safe — concurrent calls from multiple threads cause data races and unpredictable behavior.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace strtok() with strtok_r() (POSIX) or use std::string::find() and std::string::substr() for safe, re-entrant tokenization.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3: DES, 3DES, RC4, RC2, and Blowfish are not FIPS 140-3 approved and are cryptographically weak.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with AES-256-GCM (EVP_aes_256_gcm()) via the OpenSSL EVP interface as required by FIPS 140-3.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / CWE-327: AES in ECB mode is not semantically secure — identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext, and it provides no authentication.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with EVP_aes_256_gcm() which provides authenticated encryption (AEAD) as required by FIPS 140-3.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded secrets detected in C++ source — exposure in version control, logs, or compiled binaries is a critical risk.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove hardcoded secrets. Use environment variables, a secrets manager (e.g., HashiCorp Vault), or an encrypted configuration store.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-544 / CWE-111: longjmp() and siglongjmp() bypass C++ destructors and RAII, causing resource leaks, undefined behavior, and potential security vulnerabilities.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove all uses of longjmp() from C++ code. Use C++ exceptions (throw/catch) for non-local error handling instead.
